page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.g7 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates on the KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.g7.xlarge delivers moderate single-core performance but exhibits limitations under multi-threaded workloads. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is rated as average, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also fall within the average range. However, multi-core performance is weaker, as evidenced by a weak multi-core stress-ng CPU score and a poor rating for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, with both large-block read and write speeds categorized as weak.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark characteristics, the ecs.g7.xlarge is suited for general-purpose workloads that do not require high-throughput multi-threaded processing or local disk storage. Appropriate use cases include light web serving, basic application hosting, and moderate database operations. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a standard resource density for general-purpose computing, though workloads requiring high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-core execution may experience performance bottlenecks.
